title: Refund Sequence between a Resident Funds Transfer and Other Payments on an Ancillary Charge
content:
When part of an ancillary charge is refundable because a payer covers it, and the charge was paid partly by a transfer from a Resident Trust Fund Accounts account and partly by other means, the refundable part is shared between the transfer and the charge's other payments in the refund order. The charge's other payments are the payments naming it by check, ACH or card on the resident's Ancillary and Optional Services Billing account. The refund order sets **the transfer's portion** of the refundable part, from which the return to the resident funds account is figured.

## The refund order

The first row that fits decides.

| When the charge's other payments were made | Transfer's portion |
|---|---|
| a payment other than the transfer named the charge on a later date than the transfer | the other payments are refunded first; the transfer's portion is what remains of the refundable part after them, never below zero |
| another payment named the charge on the transfer's own date | the refundable part multiplied by the transfer's paid part, divided by the paid part plus the other payments |
| otherwise | the whole refundable part |

## Hypothetical illustration

Refundable part $90.00; transfer's paid part $60.00; other payments by check $40.00.

| Date of the check | Transfer's portion |
|---|---|
| after the transfer | $90.00 less $40.00: $50.00 |
| same day as the transfer | $90.00 times 60.00 divided by 100.00: $54.00 |
| before the transfer | $90.00 |

With other payments of $110.00 made after the transfer, nothing remains for the transfer: its portion is $0.00.
